title: Short-run burn and margin stress test (hosted API)
body:
Purpose:
- Quick spreadsheet to sanity-check 3 short-run scenarios (base, surge, crash) and show impact on cash burn and margin for hosted API over next 6 months. Not final; working assumptions in yellow.

SHEET: Monthly P&L (months = Sep25 -> Feb26)
Columns: Month | Tiered Tokens (m) | Avg Price /k tokens (USD) | Gross Rev (USD) | GPU amortization (committed) | Burst GPU cost (on-demand) | Network/storage COGS | Cache savings | Net COGS | Gross Margin | Gross Margin % | Notes
Row BASE: Sep-25 | 120 | 0.38 | =120*1000*0.38 -> 45,600 | 18,000 | 1,200 | 3,000 | -2,500 | =18000+1200+3000-2500 -> 19,700 | =45600-19700 = 25,900 | 56.9% | steady growth, normal SLO
Row SURGE: Oct-25 | 200 | 0.35 | 70,000 | 18,000 | 8,400 | 5,000 | -4,800 | 26,600 | 43,400 | 62.0% | burst used, some on-demand GPUs, caching helps but latency higher
Row CRASH: Nov-25 | 35 | 0.40 | 14,000 | 18,000 | 0 | 900 | -700 | 18,200 | -4,200 | -30% | underutilizing reserved capacity -> negative margin
Notes on formulaic approach:
- Revenue calc: tokens (millions) * 1,000 * price_per_k.
- GPU amortization = reserved_capacity_monthly_commit / allocation_to_hosted (manual input, can be reallocated). In base we peg 18k/mo per slice.
- Burst GPU cost approximated from cloud list + ops overlay, expressed as monthly on-demand invoice for extra hours.
- Cache savings entered as negative COGS (savings reduce net COGS).

SHEET: Per-model micro-PPK mapping (sample rows)
Cols: Model | Perf class | avg tokens per request | token-weighted ppk (USD) | infra ppk reserved | infra ppk burst | total infra ppk | markup target | price ppk -> notes
Row: redwood-v1-7b | low | 225 | 0.014 | 0.006 | 0.009 | 0.015 | 0.030 -> tiered at 3c per 1k tokens equivalent
Row: redwood-v1-13b | med | 420 | 0.025 | 0.010 | 0.018 | 0.028 | 0.045 | high memory footprint, benefits from quantization after patch
Row: openfast-70b | high | 1200 | 0.095 | 0.045 | 0.072 | 0.117 | 0.160 | fallback for latency-critical flows expensive on burst
Assumptions: ppk = per 1k tokens. Multiply by request size to get per-request infra cost. Markup target is pre-tax to reach target gross margin.

SHEET: Burst sizing & amortization sensitivity (matrix)
- Axis X = reserved capacity slices (small/medium/large) expressed as GPU-hours committed per month (e.g., 4k, 8k, 16k hrs).
- Axis Y = short-term surge multiplier (1.0, 1.5, 2.5, 4.0).
- Cell = projected on-demand spend + underused amortization drag.
Quick callouts from matrix:
- Committed 4k hrs + surge x4 -> huge on-demand add (~$45k) vs 16k committed reduces on-demand to ~$6k but increases amortization drag when utilization low.
- Break-even surge multiplier for 8k commit is ~2.2x for typical token mix.

SHEET: Latency SLO penalty and fallback cost
- Model routing policy: prefer cheaper model within 50ms margin. If >SLO, route to fast small model (higher ppk in aggregate due to quality retries).
- Example: 90th pct latency target 180ms. If heavy load pushes primary 13b latencies to 240ms -> 30% of requests rerouted to redwood-v1-7b with more decoding steps -> effective ppk increase + 8% extra tokens due to verbose fallback.
- Add a row: SLO breach cost = reroute_volume * (ppk_fallback - ppk_primary) + additional token inflation.

OPEN ITEMS / QUESTIONS (working):
- How to account for committed GPU license/infra discounts that are applied quarterly vs monthly? (affects month-to-month burn)
- Should we forecast cache hit improvements from token-level prefix caching as a phased ramp (week 1: 8% hit -> week 8: 23%)? Current sheet uses flat -20% savings for baseline. Need product input.
- Treatment of data egress for embeddings-heavy customers: currently lumped into network/storage COGS; ask infra to split by customer segment.

ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS (short):
- Aisha: get month-by-month reserved contract amortization schedule (ticket RED-504). Deadline: 2025-09-12.
- Jonah: run quick empirical job to measure average token inflation when falling back across 10 prod flows. Add numbers to per-model sheet. Deadline: 2025-09-09.
- Liam: add a shaded scenario that pro-rates quarterly license credits into months for 3 possible recognition policies (front-load, straight-line, back-load).

MINI SENSITIVITY PASTE (for quick copy into other sheets):
- Delta margin per 1k tokens when burst on-demand cost moves +$0.005/ppk = -5 percentage points at 100m tokens/mo revenue bucket.
- If cache hit improves from 20% -> 30% on high-volume customers, expected reduction in net COGS ~ 6k/mo for 100m tokens bucket.

ROUGH UX NOTES (for product ops):
- Consider adding a dashboard tile: committed utilization %, projected on-demand next 48h, projected burn delta if surge > threshold.
- Alert rule: if projected margin < 25% in next 7 days for >=1 region, auto-suggest: (1) enable conservative batching, (2) temporarily raise price floor for new customers, (3) enable model-fallback policy to cheaper family.

VERSION LOG:
- 2025-09-02 initial draft (Liam)
- 2025-09-04 added per-model ppk mapping (Sofia)
- 2025-09-08 inserted burst matrix and quick numbers (Aisha)
- 2025-09-10 updated open items and added next steps (Liam)

Notes to self: this sheet is intentionally light on legal/contract language. For any recommendations that change committed capacity we must loop in finance and SRE (tickets: FIN-318, SRE-2025).

Scratch area (raw numbers to iterate):
- Reserved amortization buckets tested: 12k/mo = $40k, 8k/mo = $28k, 4k/mo = $15k (these are ballpark including infra + license).
- On-demand price per effective GPU-hour used in sheet: $7.5 - $9.8 depending on family. Add markup for infra ops (~10%).
- Typical avg request tokens across pilot customers: 180 - 540 (skewed right).

End of sheet.
